messages:
raj: Hey team, hitting a sustained stream of 429s from our Dedicated pool since ~15:03 UTC. TPS shot from 120 -> 520 for ~6m, tokens/sec SLO violated. Customers reporting degraded chat UX. Can provide logs.

carmen: Sorry you're seeing that, raj. Can you paste one example request + response headers and the pool name? Also which model variant?

raj: pool: redwood-dedicated-nyc-3, model: llama-13b-q4. Example: 
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Reason: admission_control
X-Burst-Credits-Remaining: 0
X-Pool-Headroom: 0
Retry-After: 15
```
We saw admission_control in the header and X-Burst-Credits-Remaining=0. This started right after a marketing campaign spike.

carmen: ok that header is helpful. Did you see any autoscaler events in your console? Any queued requests?

raj: Console shows many queued but autoscale didn't add nodes. Pool config shows min_replicas: 2, max_replicas: 20, current_replicas: 2. Incident start 15:02, spike peaked 15:08.

alerts-bot: [ALERT] Admission Control fired on pool redwood-dedicated-nyc-3 at 2026-03-12T15:04:23Z — token_ps exceeded threshold. Burst credits exhausted.

drew: Noted. Quick hypothesis: burst credits drained due to sudden sustained TPS; admission control caps tps to protect latency SLOs. Autoscaler may not have scaled because the scale signal (cpu/gpu util) didn't yet exceed threshold or the scale cooldown prevented growth.

carmen: Raj — can you run a repro with a low-rate ramp that emits headers? Example script below to capture X-Burst-Credits-Remaining and Retry-After: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | egrep -i 'X-Burst-Credits|Retry-After'
  sleep 0.5
done
```
Post outputs if you can.

raj: Will run now, attaching a short excerpt: 
```
X-Burst-Credits-Remaining: 3
X-Burst-Credits-Remaining: 1
X-Burst-Credits-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 20
```
So credits went to zero within ~10s of sustained ramp.

kevin: Two immediate mitigations: 1) Increase pool burst_budget by +600 tokens/sec for 1 hour to buy headroom, 2) Temporarily bump min_replicas to 4 to give autoscaler time to catch up. I can patch via infra CLI if you approve.

carmen: Also check request mix — long-context requests consume many tokens and deplete credits faster. Any sudden shift to long history?

raj: No, payload lengths similar to baseline. It's pure TPS spike from new campaign.

drew: I'll check autoscaler logs. Possible root cause: scale_up cooldown = 300s and our signal was flaky because admission control throttled the GPU-util metric reporting; autoscaler didn't see sustained util > threshold. If true we need a quick follow-up: emit synthetic metric when admission_control fires so autoscaler treats it as a scale signal.

kevin: For short-term: @carmen please approve increasing burst_budget and min_replicas. Also we'll create a routing fallback: route 20% of requests to regional-fallback pool to reduce burst.

carmen: Approved. kevin — go ahead. raj — can you confirm if routing fallback is ok for your SLA while we stabilize?

raj: Yes, fallback acceptable for 30m window. Please coordinate.

alerts-bot: [ACTION] kevin increased redwood-dedicated-nyc-3:burst_budget by 600 at 2026-03-12T15:18:41Z. min_replicas set to 4.

kevin: Patch applied. Monitoring now. Early signs: 429 rate dropping, burst credits slowly recovering. Still watching admission_control events.

carmen: Thanks. For the postmortem we need: 1) exact timeline, 2) autoscaler cooldown behavior and metrics, 3) burst budget sizing guidance, 4) a playbook for temporary routing.

drew: I'll collect autoscaler logs and propose a fix: when Admission Control triggers, emit a synthetic autoscale metric AND reduce scale cooldown to 60s for that pool as an emergency path.

raj: Confirmed UX improved at 15:22. We'll keep increased capacity for 45m then rollback. Appreciate the fast response.

carmen: Created support ticket SUP-2026-0143 and routed to eng-sre for longer-term changes. Next steps: eng-sre to own follow-up, support to send customer update, product to consider configuring default burst buffers for onboarding.

kevin: Adding one more note — recommend pre-warming for planned campaigns: reserve burst credits and increase min_replicas an hour before. I'll draft a short KB article.

carmen: Closing thread when postmortem draft posted. :white_check_mark:
